I found several GitHub issues on this topic. Most are about browser extensions or plugins injecting markup that React then flags as a mismatch.

- **Newest React issue:** facebook/react #36169 reports that a `<script defer>` inside `<head>` triggers hydration warnings on React 19.2.4. The issue's error text also says extensions that alter the HTML before React loads can cause this, and the issue is still open.
- **Older React issues:** facebook/react #25924, a React 18.2 report, traces intermittent hydration errors to a script tag that the React DevTools extension injects after the body. It asks whether the extension should use `suppressHydrationWarning`. facebook/react #24430 describes a similar case, where a plugin inserts a script tag above `<head>`. Its status is Backlog.
- **React's stated position:** A Video Speed Controller issue quotes React's position that extensions should mostly avoid generating unexpected HTML. Its quoted React 19 blog text says unexpected tags in `<head>` and `<body>` are skipped, though stylesheets from extensions can be left in place if React re-renders the whole document. (The quote comes from a third-party issue, so check react.dev for the exact wording.)
- **Attribute injection:** Next.js discussion #72035 found that the `cz-shortcut-listen` attribute from the ColorZilla extension caused the mismatch. Users worked around it by removing the attribute before hydration or by disabling the extension. facebook/react #31658 cites a `data-np-intersection-state` attribute, but it was closed as not planned after going stale.
- **Other tools:** A Sentry issue (#15886) shows that suppressing React 19's hydration error through Sentry's ignore rules did not work. A Video Speed Controller issue (#1255) traces the mismatch to a `class` attribute the extension adds to `<html>`.

Overall, the search results show no single fix. The common workarounds are disabling the extension, testing in incognito, or removing the injected attribute before hydration. The results don't include a resolution from the React team for the `<script defer>` case.

content.text:
Yes, there are several. None of them is a single canonical React 19 issue about browser extensions.

**Closest matches in facebook/react**
- [#36169](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/36169) is a hydration mismatch on `<script defer>` inside `<head>`, reported on React 19.2.4. The error text mentions extensions that alter the HTML before React loads. It is still open.
- [#25924](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/25924) says scripts injected by browser extensions, such as React DevTools, can cause hydration errors. It was filed against React 18.2, so it predates 19, but it is the clearest "extensions cause this" report.
- [#24430](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/24430) covers plugins that insert a script tag above `<head>`. Its status is Backlog.
- [#31658](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/31658) cites an extension-injected `data-np-intersection-state` attribute. It was closed as not planned after going stale.

**Related reports in other repos**
- [Next.js discussion #72035](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035) is a Next.js 15 / React 19 hydration error caused by the `cz-shortcut-listen="true"` attribute that the ColorZilla extension injects.
- [videospeed #1255](https://github.com/igrigorik/videospeed/issues/1255) is a hydration error in the Video Speed Controller extension, which adds a class to `<html>`.
- [sentry-javascript #15886](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-javascript/issues/15886) found that Sentry's ignore rules didn't suppress React 19's hydration error.

**Workarounds**
- Disable the extension, or test in incognito.
- Add `suppressHydrationWarning` on the affected element.
- Remove the injected attribute before hydration.

React's stated position is that extensions should avoid injecting unexpected HTML. I got that from a third-party issue quoting the React 19 blog post, not from the post itself, so check react.dev for the exact wording.

- https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035
